strengths: Good: The 2x2 register-blocking design is feasible and well-grounded. The arithmetic-intensity argument is textbook: with RB_M=RB_N=2, one K-block now funds 4 MMAs (32768 FLOP) from 4 coopmat_loads instead of 1 MMA (8192 FLOP) from 2 loads — a 4x FLOP-to-load ratio improvement that directly relieves the issue/bandwidth bottleneck diagnosed in §3.1.16. This is the same 'register blocking' strategy used in NVIDIA's CUTLASS GemmUniversal and the Triton matmul tutorial to amortize shared-memory loads.

Good: The codegen non-change claim is verified directly from source. detect_loop_carried_coopmat (body.rs:932-990) iterates ALL coopmat_binding_ids, sorts by BindingId for determinism, then pushes (bid, phi_id) for every binding that satisfies the unconditional top-level reassign criteria. emit_for_range steps 3/5/7/10/11 use PARALLEL Vecs (pre_header_values, latch_values, carried) that are fully general for N. Step 10 (body.rs:1173-1246) inserts in REVERSE declaration order via InsertPoint::Begin so the phis end up in declaration order at indices 0..N — compliant with SPIR-V Unified Specification §2.4 ('All OpPhi instructions must appear before all other instructions in a block'). AT-1702 verified this mechanism for 2 phis across 2 NESTED loops; the same Vec machinery trivially handles N=4 phis in ONE loop (no structural difference in the emit path). AT-1733 is the right new test to LOCK this guarantee before the kernel ships.

Good: The N-phi single-loop path has no ordering or dominance corner case. In a single-loop scenario with N=4 accumulators, each OpPhi references exactly the same two predecessor labels (pre_header_label and continue_label) — there is no nested-loop ambiguity about which continue block is the latch. The reverse-order BeginInsert correctly produces declaration order for any N, and all phis share the same predecessor pair. SPIR-V spec §3.32.11 (OpPhi) requires only that each (value, label) pair identifies a predecessor block, which all N phis satisfy identically.

Good: Multi-subgroup deferral is confirmed by direct code inspection. axc-hir/src/subgroup.rs enumerates ONLY: InvocationId (SubgroupLocalInvocationId), Size (SubgroupSize), Elect, Reduce variants, BroadcastFirst, All, Any. There is no LocalInvocationId, SubgroupId, or NumSubgroups variant. The grep result is authoritative — there is literally no HIR node for these builtins, so the deferral is honest and the path to unblock it (a new SubgroupOp variant + SPIR-V BuiltIn LocalInvocationId Input variable lowering, mirroring the existing GlobalInvocationId path in buffers.rs) is well-scoped.

Good: Shared-memory sizing is well within limits. 2x2: A-block = 2*16*16*2 = 1024 B + B-block = 2*16*16*2 = 1024 B = 2048 B total. The Vulkan spec minimum maxComputeSharedMemorySize is 16,384 B (Vulkan 1.3 spec §36.2 table); RTX PRO 6000 provides 49,152 B per SM. 2048 B is 12.5% of the minimum spec floor — no risk. 4x4 = 4096 B is 25% of the floor, still safe. The runtime SharedMemoryExceedsDeviceLimit preflight (context.rs:869) provides the fail-closed gate.

Good: The correctness oracle is mathematically sound. The argument that register blocking preserves bit-exactness is correct: each acc_ij independently accumulates coopmat_mul_add over the same K-blocks in the same order as a single-tile kernel dispatched for tile (i,j). Coopmat mul_add is order-preserving and deterministic on the same hardware. The non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, K-sum <= 2048) guarantees f16-integer-exactness per the f16 mantissa (10-bit mantissa, exact for integers up to 2048). AT-1731/1732 with max_diff==0 is the appropriate oracle.

Good: The bench design (resident_matmul_rb.rs) is a clean derivative of the AT-1710 resident_matmul_competitive.rs template, with the same honest-reporting discipline: bare TFLOPS + % only, 'competitive' label only if pct >= 25.0 (COMPETITIVE_PCT_THRESHOLD), no ratio asserted (only tflops>0 && finite), 50 GB cap + 2D grid pre-check on both axes, typed-skip on CoopMatUnsupported. The additive-not-replacing strategy (AT-1710/AT-1711 retained) preserves the baseline comparison.

Good: AT-1734 (compile + spirv-val anchor for matmul_rb_coopmat.axc in CI) ensures the SPIR-V structural validity of the new kernel is gate-checked without a real coopmat GPU — the same conservative gatekeeping pattern that protected M3.3b.

Good: The dispatch grid math is correct. For RB_M=RB_N=2 at M=N=K=256: grid = (256/32, 256/32, 1) = (8, 8, 1) = 64 workgroups. With 32 threads per workgroup that is 2048 total threads against an RTX PRO 6000 (96 SM × 2 warp schedulers each). This is well within the max_compute_work_group_count limits (Vulkan spec minimum is 65535 on each axis). The 2D pre-check on both axes guards the bench correctly.

Good: @strategy holes (rb_m, rb_n, a_block_size, b_block_size) are GENUINELY used — they drive the shared-array literal sizes (shared a_tile: shared[f16, ?a_block_size]) and the bench dispatch grid. This satisfies the anti-pattern-5 rule (annotations as first-class data) and directly addresses the M3.1.5 inert-holes postmortem.
concerns: Minor: In HN-5, the staging index math for the B-tile is computed with a hard-coded divisor of 32 for b_row (b_row=ei/32) where 32 = RB_N*16 for RB_N=2. This is consistent and correct for the 2x2 variant, but the comment in the technical_spec notes this is 'generalized from M3.3b' — Coder must be alert that this divisor is RB_N*16, not a literal 32, when/if other RB variants are considered. For the shipped 2x2 this is unambiguous.

Minor: The open_question OQ-2 / AT-1733 is the right skeptical gate: AT-1702 proved 2 phis across 2 NESTED loops (one phi per header across two headers), while AT-1733 must prove N=4 phis in ONE single header. These are structurally different, though the code path is identical (the Vec machinery does not distinguish). The Pessimistic reviewer may want to verify that the step-10 BeginInsert loop (body.rs:1178) does not accidentally re-select a stale block index after multiple insertions. From reading the code: select_block(header_block_idx) is called ONCE before the insertion loop (body.rs:1175), then each InsertPoint::Begin inserts at position 0 of the CURRENTLY SELECTED block without re-selecting — this is correct, all N insertions go into the same header block. But this is worth the Pessimistic reviewer confirming explicitly.

Minor: tile_k FIXED at 16 is the same constraint as M3.3b and is correct, but the @strategy hint for tile_k still appears as ?[16] (a one-element candidate set). This is technically fine as a strategy hole that the bench assigns, but a reader could wonder if it ever varies. The technical_spec is clear that it does not; the coder_handoff_note HN-2 confirms this. No action needed — just a documentation clarity point.

Minor: OQ-4 asks what happens if 2x2 delivers only 7-10% uplift. The acceptance gate (tflops > 5.04, honest reporting) is correct. If the result is 7-10%, that is an honest M3.3c result: the register-blocking mechanism is validated, the TFLOPS are improved, and the multi-subgroup path (which would deliver much larger gains) is identified as the next lever. The milestone is not diminished by a modest honest number — it validates the mechanism and sets the stage for M3.3d.

OQ-1.position: ACCEPT hand-unrolled 2x2 as the expressibility boundary
OQ-1.rationale: AXIOM has no compile-time unroll over strategy holes and coopmat bindings are SSA scalars, not addressable array elements — this is a fundamental property of the HIR/codegen design, not a gap. The hand-unrolled 2x2 is the correct idiom within AXIOM's type system. The @strategy holes still drive real work (shared sizes, dispatch grid, bench selection). Shipping a single hand-written 2x2 now and tracking strategy-unroll / coopmat-array as a future language feature is exactly right. Reference: Triton's matrix multiplication tutorial also hand-unrolls small RB variants (e.g., BLOCK_M=128 hand-written with no compiler-driven unrolling over the block dimension) for the same reason — the tile shape must be a compile-time constant for register allocation.
OQ-1.recommendation: No change needed. Document the hand-unroll boundary in the .axc file header as the coder_handoff_notes already specify.

OQ-3.rationale: The deferral is forced by a hard language constraint (no LocalInvocationId builtin, confirmed by source inspection of axc-hir/src/subgroup.rs). The path to unblock it is well-defined (add SubgroupOp::LocalInvocationId + SPIR-V BuiltIn LocalInvocationId Input variable, identical pattern to GlobalInvocationId). Adding this builtin + the multi-warp shared-tile choreography + barrier-soundness proof for the expanded workgroup in M3.3c would be a significant scope expansion on top of the register-blocking win. The register-blocking gain is the dominant single-subgroup improvement; multi-subgroup blocking is the correct next milestone. Reference: NVIDIA's Tensor Core Programming Guide recommends achieving register occupancy first (blocking), then scaling warps per SM (multi-warp), then pipelining — the same order M3.3c -> M3.3d follows.
OQ-3.recommendation: No change needed. The deferral rationale is sound and documented. Track LocalInvocationId builtin as M3.3d / M3.4 prerequisite.

OQ-4.position: ACCEPT 'improved vs 5.04' as the sole gate; 7-10% is an acceptable honest M3.3c result
OQ-4.rationale: The acceptance gate (any improvement over 5.04 TFLOPS, reported honestly) is correct and matches AXIOM-Compute's honesty discipline. A 7-10% result (5.4-5.5 TFLOPS) is meaningful: it validates that (1) N coopmat phis in one loop work correctly, (2) A/B tile reuse raises arithmetic intensity as expected, and (3) the mechanism is GPU-proven on real hardware. The gap to 'competitive' (25%) would be honestly explained by the single-subgroup ceiling — that gap is the motivation for M3.3d multi-subgroup blocking. Attempting 2x4 best-effort (as the Architect recommends) is valuable: if it adds measurable gain without spilling registers, it improves the result; if it spills, it confirms the register-pressure ceiling honestly. Requiring 2x4 to ship as a BLOCKING condition would be overscoping.
OQ-4.recommendation: Accept the Architect's recommendation: ship whatever 2x2 honestly delivers + attempt 2x4 best-effort. Acceptance gate remains 'improved vs 5.04'. If the honest best is 7-10%, label it non-competitive and document multi-subgroup as the path to 25%+.

validation_against_existing: detect_loop_carried_coopmat + emit_for_range in body.rs (lines 932-1257) verified directly: the Vec-based parallel pre_header_values/latch_values/carried machinery is fully general for N. The reverse-order BeginInsert at step 10 (lines 1178-1239) correctly handles N=4 with a single select_block call before the loop.
AT-1702 (opphi_loop_carried.rs lines 253-336) confirmed to test 2 phis across 2 NESTED loops (one per header), not N phis in one header. AT-1733 correctly targets the new single-header N=4 case.

axc-hir/src/subgroup.rs confirmed: SubgroupOp enum has 7 variants — InvocationId, Size, Elect, Reduce(kind), BroadcastFirst, All, Any. No LocalInvocationId, SubgroupId, or NumSubgroups. Multi-subgroup deferral is forced, not a choice.

matmul_shared_coopmat.axc confirms the index-recovery idiom (tile_row = gid(1u32), tile_col = gid(0u32)/32u32, lane = subgroup_invocation_id()) that M3.3c extends with the RB block offset (tile_row = block_row*RB_M + i, tile_col = block_col*RB_N + j).

resident_matmul_competitive.rs confirmed as the methodology template for resident_matmul_rb.rs: COMPETITIVE_PCT_THRESHOLD=25.0, N_WARMUP=2, N_MEASURED=10, only tflops>0&&finite asserted, 50GB cap, 2D grid pre-check.
external_references: SPIR-V Unified Specification §2.4: 'All OpPhi instructions in a block must appear before all other instructions in the block (aside from OpLabel)' — the reverse-order BeginInsert satisfies this for N=4 phis. https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html

SPIR-V Unified Specification §3.32.11 (OpPhi): operands are (value, label) predecessor pairs; valid as long as each label is a predecessor block — all N phis share the same two predecessors (pre_header_label, continue_label). https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html

NVIDIA CUTLASS GemmUniversal register-blocking (GEMM Threadblock): register-blocked accumulators (Accumulator fragments held across the K-loop) are the standard CUTLASS-v2 pattern for improving arithmetic intensity on Tensor Core workloads. https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/main/media/docs/gemm_api.md

Triton matmul tutorial §3 'Register Blocking': tile shapes are compile-time constants (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) with accumulator tensors held across the K-loop, matching the hand-unrolled AXIOM pattern. https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/03-matrix-multiplication.html

Vulkan 1.3 Specification §36.2 Table: minMaxComputeSharedMemorySize = 16,384 bytes; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell provides 49,152 bytes per SM. https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html

NVIDIA Tensor Core Programming Guide (Hopper Architecture Tuning Guide): optimal matmul tuning order is (1) register blocking, then (2) multi-warp/CTA tiling, then (3) software pipelining — M3.3c -> M3.3d ordering matches this progression. https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/hopper-tuning-guide/

SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix specification: CoopMatKHR instructions are storage-class-agnostic; the load/store access chain pointer differs between Workgroup (single-index) and StorageBuffer (two-index) but the mul_add op is identical regardless of accumulator count per loop. https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Registry/blob/main/extensions/KHR/SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix.asciidoc
test_suggestions: AT-1733 is the critical path gate — run it first before proceeding to GPU tests. If it fails, stop and escalate to the Architect (per HN-3). The test structure (compile + SPIR-V binary inspection for exactly N=4 OpPhi in one loop header, distinct result ids, 2 predecessor pairs each, spirv-val exit 0) precisely targets the single structural difference vs AT-1702.

AT-1731 fixture M=N=64 with RB=2x2 (block grid 2x2) is the right minimal case: 4 workgroups each computing a 32x32 output block, exercising both the inter-block grid dispatch and the intra-block multi-accumulator accumulation. K=32 (2 K-blocks) is the load-bearing trip count for OpPhi carry.

AT-1732 K=48 (3 K-blocks) vs K=32 (2 K-blocks) correctly exercises the phi carry across different trip counts — this was the fix that proved OpPhi was working in M3.3 (AT-1707) and is equally important for the 4-phi variant.

Consider adding a simple spirv-dis or binary scan to AT-1733 that asserts the 4 phi result IDs are CONSECUTIVE (deterministically allocated by the sorted BindingId order in detect_loop_carried_coopmat). This would guard against non-determinism in phi order if the sort is ever perturbed. This is a SUGGESTION, not a requirement.

AT-1734 (compile + spirv-val with shipped RB assignments) in CI is correctly scoped — it provides the no-GPU gate. The shared_memory_bytes computation check (= (512 + 512)*2 = 2048 bytes for 2x2) should be asserted explicitly against the metadata, not just implied by spirv-val passing.
summary: M3.3c is a sound, tightly-scoped, and honest design. The register-blocking approach directly addresses the diagnosed M3.3b bottleneck (arithmetic intensity, not compiler capability), the codegen non-change claim is verified by direct source inspection of detect_loop_carried_coopmat and emit_for_range, the multi-subgroup deferral is forced by a confirmed language absence (no LocalInvocationId in axc-hir/src/subgroup.rs), the correctness oracle (bit-exact max_diff==0 on the integer-f16 fixture) is mathematically sound, and the bench honesty discipline (bare TFLOPS, no asserted ratio, 'competitive' only at >= 25%) matches the established AT-1710 template. AT-1733 is the correct pre-ship gate for the N-phi single-loop guarantee. OQ-1 (hand-unrolled 2x2 acceptable), OQ-3 (defer multi-subgroup), and OQ-4 (7-10% honest result acceptable) are all resolved in favor of the Architect's recommendations. APPROVE to proceed to Pessimistic Design Review.
